value: Study population: 35 Swedish health care students (medical, nursing, dentistry) from universities in Umeå, Stockholm, and Gothenburg
Travel destinations: Indian peninsula (n=18) and Central Africa (n=17)
Fecal specimens collected before and after travel
69% of subjects experienced traveler's diarrhea (12/17 Africa, 12/18 India)
Two-thirds (23/35) participated in hospital-based patient work
No subjects took antibiotics within 6 months prior to sampling
Sequencing: Illumina HiSeq 2000 for metagenomic data; Illumina MiSeq for ESBL isolates
178 different resistance genes detected across specimens
ESBL acquisition: 12/18 (67%) India travelers, 0/17 Africa travelers
All ESBL-positive isolates carried CTX-M-15 gene
Increased Proteobacteria in 25/35 students after travel
Median 4 days before departure and 22 days after return for specimen collection
Total sequencing: 57.7–463.8 million read pairs per library before filtering

extraction_warnings: This is a longitudinal study where each of 35 participants contributed two fecal samples (before and after travel). The schema requested sample-level extraction, but the paper does not provide individual sample identifiers or per-sample metadata. The two sample rows above represent the two collection timepoints (pre-travel and post-travel), stratified by travel destination subcohort, but individual subject/sample IDs are not available. For proper sample-level harmonization, upstream data submission systems should assign unique sample IDs.

Age, sex, and other demographic information are reported only at the cohort level (e.g., '74% females', age range 23-34 years), not per individual sample. The extracted cohort-level values are reflected in the samples rows, but true per-sample sex and age data were not available in the provided paper text.

The paper does not report individual-level antibiotic susceptibility or resistance phenotypes in the text sections provided. Resistance gene abundances and ESBL phenotypes are reported at the group/cohort level or for aggregated pre/post comparisons, not per sample.
Batch 1 returned granularity='study_level', differs from batch 0 ('sample_level'); kept batch 0.

This schema appears designed for oncology and clinical disease studies; the present paper is a microbiome study of healthy travelers with no disease state, treatment response outcomes, or tumor staging. Most fields are inapplicable.

The paper focuses on antibiotic resistance gene acquisition via travel, not treatment response or clinical outcomes. Biomarker values extracted are resistance gene abundances and fold-changes, not typical clinical response measures.
One subject had ESBL-producing E. coli before travel (from Central Africa group), but this was not detected after return, indicating loss rather than acquisition.
Study explicitly excluded subjects on antibiotic therapy within 6 months, so 'treatment' field reflects this exclusion criterion rather than active treatment.
